summary: A safety-first, suit-aware excursion map and decision-support system fusing 9 authentic NASA/USGS datasets into a 5-meter Jezero Crater grid, featuring a real-time Safe Return Envelope isochrone that guarantees the mandatory 1.5× consumables reserve.
details:
The Problem: Regional Orbiters vs. Boots on the Ground
For over two decades, NASA has explored Mars through robotic orbiters and rovers. Existing planetary mapping tools—such as JPL Mars Trek and USGS global maps—are designed for orbital scales (kilometers per pixel), making them blind to localized obstacles faced by human astronauts on the surface. When the first crew lands at Jezero Crater, they will navigate steep delta erosional scarps, boulder fields, and loose regolith dune traps while encased in pressurized suits with strict life-support consumables.
### Our Solution: Marswalk Navigator
Marswalk Navigator provides a hyperlocal, 5-meter resolution decision-support system centered on the Jezero Crater Western Delta Front (18.40°N–18.47°N, 77.40°E–77.48°E). Rather than a static academic map, it acts as an active survival guide:
1. The Safe Return Envelope (Hero Feature): A real-time radial Dijkstra isochrone flood-fill from Habitat Alpha that calculates the exact boundary crew can reach while strictly reserving NASA's mandatory 1.5× life-support margin (O2, battery, water). Crew can dial their excursion budget from 45 to 360 minutes in real time.
2. Suit-Aware A* Routing & SEXTANT Logistics: Dynamic Martian Tobler walking speeds calibrated for 0.38g surface gravity and suit stiffness (0.4–3.2 km/h), hard 15° slope impassable barriers, and 1-click toggling between Foot EVA (2 Crew) and Rover Carrier logistics (5.0 km/h, 12h aux power).
3. 3D RF Line-of-Sight (LOS): Real-time ray-marching across the elevation grid to Habitat Alpha's 10m mast identifies terrain communication blackouts.
4. Crisis Alerting & Solar Particle Event (SPE) Simulation: Simulates a coronal mass ejection shock arrival, sounding an emergency alert, contracting the safe envelope to 40 minutes, and calculating an immediate abort path to the nearest storm shelter.
5. Dual Operational Modes: Switch seamlessly between Habitat Planning Mode (tactical mission control) and High-contrast EVA HUD Visor Mode (amber/cyan heads-up display for direct sunlight readability).
6. Field Usability: Printable Astronaut Cuff Cue Cards formatted for spacesuit forearm checklists and live integration with NASA's Mars 2020 Raw Image API (579,000+ images).
